key_insight: Al-Ghasali models closed Islamic jurisprudential chapters as deterministic finite-state automata, using constrained LLMs only to verbalize computed rulings.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a design for rule-governed AI systems that separate deterministic decisions from probabilistic language generation.
method: Compile finite propositional Horn rules into deterministic automata for O(1) verdict extraction.
Compose sub-chapter automata and encode ordering requirements in explicit states.
Constrain LLM output with execution-derived grammars, a bounded neutral lexicon, and valence locking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports formal proofs of complexity preservation and conditional hallucination prevention, but provides no datasets, benchmarks, or empirical evaluation results.
watch_item: Guarantees depend on correct and complete rule formalization and faithfully implemented decoding constraints; offline compilation costs and state-space growth require scrutiny.
paper_title: Al-Ghasali: A Computational Framework for Simulating Islamic Jurisprudential Rulings via Finite State Automata and Large Language Models
